main_text.p: donià, Thraciâ, Asiâ, Oriente, Ægypto, Macedonum successorum Alexandri ar-mis varie raptatis & distractis, & in prædam versis, cum gloria Græcorum senfini decresceret, sola fere Rhodus non solum fortunam priorem servavit, sed opibus quoque & splendore, accelebritate omnique cultu crevit, ab ipso Alexandro Magno supra omnes reli-quas civitates, ut ait Diodorus, honorata: cui gloria purgati à prædonibus maris tributa fuit: à nemine ducum ac regum inter se bellantium, ac terrarum orbem turbantium tracta in partes, sed quieti relicta, & omnium amicitia am-bita: usque quò Olympiadis cxviii anno quarto, qui fuit decimus septimus à morte Alexandri, Antigonus Asiæ rex in societatem belli contra Ptolemæum in Ægypto regnantem sibi adscifcere eam conatus fuit. Quod cum ipsa primum deprecata, deinde minis gravibus tentata nihilominus recusaret, propterea quòd amicitiâ Ptolemæi frueretur, à Demetrio Antigoni filio gravissimo bel-lo petita fuit: in quod bellum præter magnum numerum vectoriarum cc na-ves longas ac armatas minores majo-resque, & militum quadragies mille, equitesque & auxiliares prædones cum omnis generis machinis bellicis ad op-pugnan-

page.notes: Left margin shows red bleed marks and the letters "ai" and "EQ" near the edge; these look like show-through or edge marks from the neighbouring page and are not transcribed. "bel-lo" at the line end is partly doubtful (the second syllable could read "to"); "am-bita" is doubtful in its first syllable. The "f"-like initial of "successorum" is a long s, read as s.
